legend.0: 0: breaks one or more accepted visible, manual, heartbeat, Stop, path, or policy gates.
legend.1: 1: preserves only a small part of the known behavior and leaves major contract gaps.
legend.2: 2: preserves several known contracts but leaves material behavior or rollback gaps.
legend.3: 3: preserves the known contracts with bounded, testable gaps and a rollback path.
legend.4: 4: preserves all stated contracts with an explicit rollback path and no new unbounded behavior.

legend.0: 0: requires a broad redesign with new frameworks or many unrelated moving parts.
legend.1: 1: requires several new subsystems and difficult coordination across them.
legend.2: 2: requires a moderate number of focused changes with some new coordination.
legend.3: 3: requires focused changes with familiar components and bounded coordination.
legend.4: 4: requires the smallest coherent change set for the endpoint.

legend.0: 0: makes ownership ambiguous and leaves common failure paths without a clear owner.
legend.1: 1: clarifies few failure paths and introduces substantial lifecycle ambiguity.
legend.2: 2: gives partial ownership clarity but leaves material crash or PID risks.
legend.3: 3: gives clear ownership for ordinary failures with bounded hardening work.
legend.4: 4: gives clear ownership, failure boundaries, and cleanup responsibilities.

legend.0: 0: needs a fragile bootstrap, broad dependency set, or incompatible output paths.
legend.1: 1: has major bootstrap or dependency distribution risk.
legend.2: 2: has a workable build with several unresolved bootstrap or cache decisions.
legend.3: 3: uses the approved paths and a bounded build sequence with minor decisions left.
legend.4: 4: uses a simple reproducible build and distribution sequence under approved paths.

legend.0: 0: cannot isolate regressions or restore the accepted baseline.
legend.1: 1: needs broad new tests before any useful rollback is possible.
legend.2: 2: supports partial isolation and rollback with material untested areas.
legend.3: 3: supports staged tests, evidence, and rollback for known contracts.
legend.4: 4: supports small staged tests, direct comparison, and a clear rollback at each step.

legend.0: 0: creates high long-term duplication or a new framework burden.
legend.1: 1: creates substantial maintenance burden across runtime and tooling.
legend.2: 2: has moderate ongoing burden and some duplicated contracts.
legend.3: 3: keeps maintenance bounded with limited duplication.
legend.4: 4: minimizes ongoing code, dependency, and contract maintenance.
